claim: FAM65B mutations cause hearing loss by an unknown mechanism.
source: FAM65B mutations cause hearing loss by an unknown mechanism.
evidence: This statement is presented in the abstract as established knowledge from prior research, supported by citation context.

claim: Fam65b oligomers form a circumferential ring near the basal taper of the mechanically sensitive stereocilia of murine hair cells.
source: Using biochemistry and stochastic optical reconstruction microscopy (STORM), we show here that Fam65b oligomers form a circumferential ring near the basal taper of the mechanically sensitive stereocilia of murine hair cells.
evidence: This claim is supported by STORM imaging data and biochemical experiments presented in the manuscript.

claim: Taperin forms a dense-core-like structure that is disrupted in the absence of Fam65b.
source: Taperin, a second protein near the taper, forms a dense-core-like structure that is disrupted in the absence of Fam65b.
evidence: This is supported by STORM imaging and immunolocalization data comparing control and Fam65b-deficient mice.

claim: Stereocilia of Fam65b-deficient murine hair cells start to develop, but mechanotransduction is affected and stereocilia deteriorate.
source: Stereocilia of Fam65b-deficient murine hair cells start to develop, but mechanotransduction is affected and stereocilia deteriorate.
evidence: This is supported by morphological analysis, SEM imaging, and electrophysiological recordings presented in the manuscript.

claim: RhoC is a Fam65b binding partner.
source: Yeast-two-hybrid screens identify RhoC as a Fam65b binding partner.
evidence: This is supported by yeast-two-hybrid screening data and co-immunoprecipitation experiments.

claim: RhoC co-localizes with Fam65b in stereocilia.
source: RhoC co-localizes with Fam65b in stereocilia and regulates Fam65b oligomerization.
evidence: This is supported by immunolocalization experiments following injectoporation of tagged constructs.

claim: RhoC regulates Fam65b oligomerization.
source: RhoC co-localizes with Fam65b in stereocilia and regulates Fam65b oligomerization.
evidence: This is supported by co-immunoprecipitation experiments showing enhanced Fam65b oligomerization in the presence of RhoC.

claim: Binding to RhoC and oligomerization are critical for Fam65b function.
source: Binding to RhoC and oligomerization are critical for Fam65b function.
evidence: This is supported by rescue experiments showing that Fam65b mutants unable to bind RhoC cannot rescue morphological defects.

claim: The membrane of stereocilia is spatially segregated into at least three domains including a specialized basal taper domain.
source: Confocal imaging of isolated bullfrog hair cells has shown that the membrane of stereocilia is spatially segregated into at least three domains including a specialized basal taper domain (Zhao et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior research.

claim: PTPRQ, USH2A and VLGR1 form extracellular filaments near the taper.
source: Cell surface receptors such as PTPRQ, USH2A and VLGR1 form extracellular filaments near the taper and recruit several cytoplasmic proteins that might link the receptors to the cytoskeleton (Adato et al., 2005; McGee et al., 2006; Michalski et al., 2007; Salles et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Myosin motor proteins such as Myo6 and Myo7A are localized near the taper.
source: Myosin motor proteins such as Myo6 and Myo7A are also localized near the taper (Hasson et al., 1997) and may be important for protein transport or for adjusting tension between the cell membrane and the cytoskeleton.
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior research and includes speculative interpretation.

claim: Radixin and taperin are concentrated at the taper region.
source: Proteins with potential roles in regulating F-actin dynamics and/or anchorage to the cell membrane such as radixin and taperin are concentrated at the taper region as well (Pataky et al., 2004; Rehman et al., 2010; Salles et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: TRIOBP forms rootlets that extend from stereocilia into the cuticular plate and traverse the taper region.
source: In addition, TRIOBP forms rootlets that extend from stereocilia into the cuticular plate and traverse the taper region (Kitajiri et al. 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior research.

claim: Mutations in genes encoding proteins localized near the taper cause inherited forms of deafness.
source: Importantly, mutations in the genes that encode proteins localized near the taper cause inherited forms of deafness (Ahmed et al., 2003; Khan et al., 2007; Liu et al., 1997; Rehman et al., 2010; Schraders et al., 2010; Weil et al., 1997), thus reinforcing the concept that the taper is a specialized and functionally important subdomain within stereocilia.
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to prior research.

claim: A mutation in FAM65B causes hearing loss in humans.
source: Recent studies have shown that a mutation in FAM65B causes hearing loss in humans (Diaz-Horta et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior research.

claim: Fam65b is expressed in hair cells.
source: Immunolocalization experiments have provided evidence that Fam65b is expressed in hair cells and knock-down of Fam65b in zebrafish leads to the loss of hair cells (Diaz-Horta et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior research.

claim: Knock-down of Fam65b in zebrafish leads to the loss of hair cells.
source: Immunolocalization experiments have provided evidence that Fam65b is expressed in hair cells and knock-down of Fam65b in zebrafish leads to the loss of hair cells (Diaz-Horta et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior research.

claim: Overexpression of Fam65b in C2C12 myoblasts and in HEK293 kidney cells leads to the formation of filopodia.
source: Accordingly, overexpression of Fam65b in C2C12 myoblasts and in HEK293 kidney cells leads to the formation of filopodia (Yoon et al., 2007), while studies in neutrophils and T-lymphocytes suggest that Fam65b can regulate RhoA activity (Gao et al., 2015; Rougerie et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior research.

claim: Fam65b can regulate RhoA activity in neutrophils and T-lymphocytes.
source: Accordingly, overexpression of Fam65b in C2C12 myoblasts and in HEK293 kidney cells leads to the formation of filopodia (Yoon et al., 2007), while studies in neutrophils and T-lymphocytes suggest that Fam65b can regulate RhoA activity (Gao et al., 2015; Rougerie et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Homozygous Fam65bLacZ/LacZ mice were deaf at 4 weeks of age.
source: Measurements of the auditory brain stem response (ABR) to broadband click stimuli in 4-week old animals revealed that homozygous mutant mice were deaf (Figure 1C,D).
evidence: This is supported by ABR measurements shown in Figure 1C,D.

claim: Fam65bLacZ/LacZ mice were deaf across the entire analyzed frequency spectrum.
source: Recordings of ABRs in response to pure tones revealed that Fam65bLacZ/LacZmice were deaf across the entire analyzed frequency spectrum (Figure 1E).
evidence: This is supported by ABR recordings shown in Figure 1E.

claim: Hearing function was minimally affected in heterozygous Fam65bLacZ/+ mice.
source: Hearing function was minimally affected in heterozygous Fam65bLacZ/+mice (Figure 1E), consistent with a recessive mode of inheritance of the auditory phenotype.
evidence: This is supported by ABR data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: DPOAEs were absent in Fam65bLacZ/LacZ mice at 4 weeks of age at all frequencies tested.
source: DPOAEs were absent in Fam65bLacZ/LacZ mice at 4 weeks of age at all frequencies tested (Figure 1F,G).
evidence: This is supported by DPOAE measurements shown in Figure 1F,G.

claim: OHC function was affected in Fam65bLacZ/LacZ mice.
source: As these emissions depend on the mechanical activity of OHCs, we conclude that OHC function was affected in Fam65bLacZ/LacZ mice.
evidence: This is inferred from the absence of DPOAEs, which depend on OHC function.

claim: The Fam65b gene was expressed along the entire length of the cochlear duct.
source: The Fam65b gene was expressed along the entire length of the cochlear duct (Figure 2A) with strongest expression in inner hair cells (IHCs), OHCs and Hensen's cells (Figure 2B,C).
evidence: This is supported by X-gal staining shown in Figure 2A-C.

claim: Fam65b gene was most strongly expressed in inner hair cells (IHCs), OHCs and Hensen's cells.
source: The Fam65b gene was expressed along the entire length of the cochlear duct (Figure 2A) with strongest expression in inner hair cells (IHCs), OHCs and Hensen's cells (Figure 2B,C).
evidence: This is supported by X-gal staining shown in Figure 2B,C.

claim: A new Fam65b splice isoform lacks amino acids encoded by exon13.
source: During cloning of the full-length Fam65b cDNA from an inner ear cDNA library, we identified a new Fam65b splice isoform that lacks amino acids encoded by exon13.
evidence: This is based on molecular cloning experiments.

claim: Expression of the smaller Fam65b isoform was detected in many tissues including the cochlea.
source: We detected by RT-PCR expression of the smaller Fam65b isoform in many tissues including the cochlea, while expression of the larger isoform was confined to the brain including the cerebellum, spinal cord and retina (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is supported by RT-PCR data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Expression of the larger Fam65b isoform was confined to the brain including the cerebellum, spinal cord and retina.
source: We detected by RT-PCR expression of the smaller Fam65b isoform in many tissues including the cochlea, while expression of the larger isoform was confined to the brain including the cerebellum, spinal cord and retina (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is supported by RT-PCR data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Fam65b was expressed in OHCs and IHCs where it outlined the shape of the stereociliary bundle.
source: In whole mounts of the cochlea at P5, we observed expression in OHCs and IHCs where Fam65b immunoreactivity outlined the shape of the stereociliary bundle (Figure 2E).
evidence: This is supported by immunohistochemistry shown in Figure 2E.

claim: Fam65b was expressed in the microvilli on the apical surface of Hensen's cells.
source: Additional staining was observed in the microvilli on the apical surface of Hensen's cells (Figure 2E), which was consistent with the X-gal staining results (Figure 2A–C).
evidence: This is supported by immunohistochemistry shown in Figure 2E.

claim: Fam65b was expressed in IHCs and OHCs at the basal end of stereocilia near the taper region.
source: Higher resolution images showed that Fam65b was expressed in IHCs and OHCs at the basal end of stereocilia near the taper region (Figure 2F).
evidence: This is supported by immunolocalization data shown in Figure 2F.

claim: HA-Fam65b was concentrated near the base of stereocilia when expressed in hair cells.
source: Consistent with the immunolocalization data using Fam65b antibodies, HA-Fam65b was concentrated near the base of stereocilia (Figure 2G).
evidence: This is supported by injectoporation experiments shown in Figure 2G.

claim: HA-Fam65b carrying a deletion linked to deafness in humans (Δ58–111) was distributed diffusely throughout the cytoplasm and no longer targeted to the base of stereocilia.
source: When we expressed by injectoporation a HA-Fam65b construct carrying a deletion linked to deafness in humans (Δ58–111), (Diaz-Horta et al., 2014), the protein was distributed diffusely throughout the cytoplasm and no longer targeted to the base of stereocilia (Figure 2H).
evidence: This is supported by injectoporation experiments shown in Figure 2H and citation to prior research.

claim: Taperin is localized near the basal taper of stereocilia.
source: Previous studies have shown that taperin is localized near the basal taper of stereocilia (Rehman et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior research.

claim: Both Fam65b and taperin showed a similar distribution near the basal taper of stereocilia.
source: To further define the localization of Fam65b, we compared in histological sections the expression pattern of Fam65b with the expression pattern of taperin. Both proteins showed a similar distribution near the basal taper of stereocilia (Figure 2I,J).
evidence: This is supported by immunolocalization data shown in Figure 2I,J.

claim: Fam65b and taperin were co-localized near the taper of stereocilia.
source: Co-staining of the hair cells with an antibody to taperin and an antibody to HA confirmed that Fam65b and taperin were co-localized near the taper of stereocilia (Figure 2K).
evidence: This is supported by co-staining experiments shown in Figure 2K.

claim: The sensory epithelium in Fam65bLacZ/LacZ mutant mice was patterned properly into three rows of OHCs and one row of IHCs at P2.
source: Whole mount staining at P2 revealed that the sensory epithelium in mutant mice was patterned properly into three rows of OHCs and one row of IHCs (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is supported by whole mount staining shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Hair bundle morphology appeared abnormal in Fam65bLacZ/LacZ mutants with aberrant bundle shape relative to controls at P2.
source: However, hair bundle morphology appeared abnormal in the mutants with aberrant bundle shape relative to controls (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is supported by whole mount staining shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Hair bundles in Fam65bLacZ/LacZ mutants contained a single kinocilium as well as a bundle of stereocilia but the bundles were abnormally shaped at P2.
source: Analysis by scanning electron microscopy (SEM) confirmed that hair bundles in the mutants contained a single kinocilium as well as a bundle of stereocilia but the bundles were abnormally shaped (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is supported by SEM analysis shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Some OHCs showed defects in hair bundle polarity at P2 in Fam65bLacZ/LacZ mutants.
source: At P2 the bundles of most OHCs appeared similar in size to wild-type and formed a staircase pattern but some OHCs showed defects in hair bundle polarity (Figure 3A,B).
evidence: This is supported by whole mount staining and SEM shown in Figure 3A,B.

claim: Hair bundles of most IHCs were severely disorganized at P2 in Fam65bLacZ/LacZ mutants.
source: In contrast, hair bundles of most IHCs were already severely disorganized (Figure 3A,B).
evidence: This is supported by whole mount staining and SEM shown in Figure 3A,B.

claim: Bundle orientation of OHCs was far more variable in Fam65bLacZ/LacZ mice compared to control heterozygous Fam65bLacZ/+ mice.
source: Unlike in control heterozygous Fam65bLacZ/+ mice, bundle orientation of OHCs was far more variable in Fam65bLacZ/LacZ mice (Figure 3F).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative analysis shown in Figure 3F.

claim: By P5 the bundles of both OHCs and IHCs were severely disorganized in Fam65bLacZ/LacZ mutants.
source: By P5 the bundles of both OHCs and IHCs were severely disorganized and many stereocilia appeared abnormally thick and large indicating that their elongation was affected (Figure 3C,D).
evidence: This is supported by whole mount staining and SEM shown in Figure 3C,D.

claim: Many stereocilia appeared abnormally thick and large at P5 in Fam65bLacZ/LacZ mutants, indicating that their elongation was affected.
source: By P5 the bundles of both OHCs and IHCs were severely disorganized and many stereocilia appeared abnormally thick and large indicating that their elongation was affected (Figure 3C,D).
evidence: This is supported by SEM analysis shown in Figure 3C,D and includes interpretation of the data.

claim: Most of the hair bundles of IHCs from Fam65bLacZ/LacZ mutant animals were disorganized and grew abnormally long when cultured in vitro.
source: When we prepared cochlear explants from Fam65bLacZ/+ and Fam65bLacZ/LacZ mice at P2 and cultured them for 2 days, most of the hair bundles of IHCs from mutant animals were disorganized and grew abnormally long (Figure 3G) indicating that bundle cohesion and growth were affected.
evidence: This is supported by in vitro culture experiments shown in Figure 3G.

claim: Bundle cohesion and growth were affected in Fam65bLacZ/LacZ mutants.
source: When we prepared cochlear explants from Fam65bLacZ/+ and Fam65bLacZ/LacZ mice at P2 and cultured them for 2 days, most of the hair bundles of IHCs from mutant animals were disorganized and grew abnormally long (Figure 3G) indicating that bundle cohesion and growth were affected.
evidence: This is inferred from the in vitro culture experiments shown in Figure 3G.

claim: Hair bundles were disorganized in Fam65bLacZ/LacZ mutant animals at P5.
source: Low magnification views revealed that hair bundles were disorganized in the mutant animals (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is supported by SEM analysis shown in Figure 4A.

claim: For OHCs, class II bundle-morphology was most prevalent at P5 in Fam65bLacZ/LacZ mutants.
source: Quantification revealed that for OHCs class II bundle-morphology was most prevalent at this age, while for IHCs class II and IIIa/b bundles were the most prominent (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is supported by quantification of SEM data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: For IHCs, class II and IIIa/b bundles were the most prominent at P5 in Fam65bLacZ/LacZ mutants.
source: Quantification revealed that for OHCs class II bundle-morphology was most prevalent at this age, while for IHCs class II and IIIa/b bundles were the most prominent (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is supported by quantification of SEM data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: The basal region of stereocilia in Fam65bLacZ/LacZ mutants was narrow and elongated.
source: Unlike in the stereocilia in wild-type mice (Figure 4D,E), the basal region of stereocilia in mutants was narrow and elongated (Figure 4F–J).
evidence: This is supported by SEM analysis shown in Figure 4F-J.

claim: Protrusions from the apical surface of hair cells were observed in Fam65bLacZ/LacZ mutants by SEM and TEM.
source: We also observed in the mutants protrusions from the apical surface of hair cells by SEM (Figure 4K,L) and transmission electron microscopy (TEM) (Figure 4M) indicative of structural changes in the apical hair cell surface.
evidence: This is supported by SEM and TEM analysis shown in Figure 4K,L,M.

claim: Hair cells with abnormal hair bundles were maintained with little evidence for hair cell loss at P16 and P28 in Fam65bLacZ/LacZ mutants.
source: Despite these strucutal abnormalities, analysis of sensory epithelia in mice at P16 and P28 revealed that hair cells with abnormal hair bundles were maintained with little evidence for hair cell loss (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by analysis shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: Taperin was no longer localized to the base of stereocilia in IHCs from Fam65bLacZ/LacZ mice.
source: Interestingly, taperin was no longer localized to the base of stereocilia in IHCs from Fam65bLacZ/LacZ mice, while the normal distribution of espin near the tips of stereocilia (Zheng et al., 2014) was maintained (Figure 5A,B).
evidence: This is supported by immunolocalization data shown in Figure 5A,B.

claim: The normal distribution of espin near the tips of stereocilia was maintained in Fam65bLacZ/LacZ mice.
source: Interestingly, taperin was no longer localized to the base of stereocilia in IHCs from Fam65bLacZ/LacZ mice, while the normal distribution of espin near the tips of stereocilia (Zheng et al., 2014) was maintained (Figure 5A,B).
evidence: This is supported by immunolocalization data shown in Figure 5A,B and citation to prior research.

claim: shRNA targeting Fam65b efficiently knocked down Fam65b-GFP expression in transfected HEK293 cells in a dose-dependent manner.
source: We generated an shRNA targeting Fam65b, which knocked down Fam65b expression in HEK293 cells in a dose-dependent manner (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: Expression of shRNA targeting Fam65b severely affected hair bundle morphology in OHCs.
source: Expression of the shRNA targeting Fam65b but not of a scrambled control shRNA severely affected hair bundle morphology (Figure 5D).
evidence: This is supported by injectoporation experiments shown in Figure 5D.

claim: Fam65b acts at least in part cell autonomously in hair cells to regulate hair bundle morphogenesis.
source: We thus conclude that Fam65b acts at least in part cell autonomously in hair cells to regulate hair bundle morphogenesis.
evidence: This is inferred from the shRNA knockdown experiments.

claim: Mechanotransduction currents could be evoked in OHCs from Fam65bLacZ/LacZ mice but peak currents were reduced.
source: Mechanotransduction currents could also be evoked in OHCs from Fam65bLacZ/LacZ mice but peak currents were reduced (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is supported by electrophysiological recordings shown in Figure 6A.

claim: The amplitude of saturated mechanotransduction currents at maximal deflection was 417.16 ± 103.77 pA for control OHCs and 232.60 ± 123.75 pA for OHCs from Fam65bLacZ/LacZ mutant mice.
source: The amplitude of saturated mechanotransduction currents at maximal deflection was at 417.16 ± 103.77 pA (mean ± SEM) for control OHCs and 232.60 ± 123.75 pA (mean ± SEM) for OHCs from mutant mice (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is supported by electrophysiological data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: The displacement-P0 curve in Fam65bLacZ/LacZ mutant animals was slightly shifted to the right and broadened.
source: The resulting curve in the mutant animals was slightly shifted to the right and broadened (Figure 6C).
evidence: This is supported by electrophysiological data shown in Figure 6C.

claim: The resting potential was comparable in OHCs from control and Fam65bLacZ/LacZ mutant animals.
source: The resting potential was comparable in OHCs from control and mutant animals (data not shown), suggesting that the change in transduction and in the displacement- P0 relationship was not a simple consequence of hair cell deterioration alone.
evidence: This is based on electrophysiological measurements.

claim: The response to fluid-jet stimulation in Fam65b-deficient hair cells was significantly decreased compared to control.
source: Hair cells from control mice responded with a robust increase in fluorescence, while the response in Fam65b-deficient hair cells was significantly decreased (Figure 6D,E).
evidence: This is supported by Ca2+ imaging data shown in Figure 6D,E.

claim: Expression of HA-Fam65b in Fam65b-deficient hair cells restored transduction to similar levels as in controls.
source: Expression of HA-Fam65b in Fam65b-deficient hair cells restored transduction to similar levels as in controls (Figure 6D,E).
evidence: This is supported by Ca2+ imaging data shown in Figure 6D,E.

claim: Expression of HA-Fam65b rescued the morphological defects in hair cells from Fam65b-deficient mice.
source: Expression of HA-Fam65b did not affect the morphology of control hair cells but it rescued the morphological defects in hair cells from Fam65b-deficient mice (Figure 6F).
evidence: This is supported by immunohistochemistry shown in Figure 6F.

claim: Fam65b is required cell autonomously in hair cells to regulate their morphology and function.
source: These findings provide further evidence that Fam65b is required cell autonomously in hair cells to regulate their morphology and function, and show that functional defects can be repaired even in hair cells at early postnatal ages.
evidence: This is inferred from the rescue experiments.

claim: Functional defects in Fam65b-deficient hair cells can be repaired even at early postnatal ages.
source: These findings provide further evidence that Fam65b is required cell autonomously in hair cells to regulate their morphology and function, and show that functional defects can be repaired even in hair cells at early postnatal ages.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the rescue experiments.

claim: Fam65b appeared as punctate dots that formed a circumferential ring outlining the edges of individual stereocilia.
source: At higher magnifications only accessible via STORM, Fam65b appeared as punctate dots that formed a circumferential ring outlining the edges of individual stereocilia (Figure 7B,C).
evidence: This is supported by STORM imaging shown in Figure 7B,C.

claim: Taperin appeared as dense puncta that extended into the core of stereocilia.
source: In contrast, taperin appeared as dense puncta that extended into the core of stereocilia (Figure 7E,F).
evidence: This is supported by STORM imaging shown in Figure 7E,F.

claim: The ring-like Fam65b structure had a diameter of 229 ± 7 nm.
source: The ring-like Fam65b structure had a diameter of 229 ± 7 nm (mean ± SEM; n=41), while the taperin structure had a diameter of 228 ± 9 nm (mean ± SEM; n=56).
evidence: This is based on measurements from STORM images.

claim: The taperin structure had a diameter of 228 ± 9 nm.
source: The ring-like Fam65b structure had a diameter of 229 ± 7 nm (mean ± SEM; n=41), while the taperin structure had a diameter of 228 ± 9 nm (mean ± SEM; n=56).
evidence: This is based on measurements from STORM images.

claim: Fam65b-GFP did not interact with HA-taperin, HA-CLIC5, HA-radixin, or HA-whirlin in co-immunoprecipitation experiments.
source: Immunoprecipitation experiments did not reveal any interactions between Fam65b-GFP with HA-taperin, HA-CLIC5, HA-radixin, HA-whirlin, and HA-PTPRQcyto (Figure 7G, and data not shown).
evidence: This is supported by co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 7G.

claim: No interaction was observed between HA-Fam65b and Myc-taperin in CL4 cells.
source: To further confirm these findings, we also expressed HA-Fam65 and Myc-taperin in CL4 cells but did not observe an interaction between the two proteins (Figure 7—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1.

claim: No interaction was observed between Fam65b and taperin in a yeast-two-hybrid assay.
source: Similarly, we did not observe interaction between Fam65b and taperin in a two-hybrid assay where we used Fam65b as a bait and taperin as a prey (Figure 7—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by yeast-two-hybrid data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1.

claim: Fam65b-GFP efficiently co-immunoprecipitated with HA-Fam65b, demonstrating that Fam65b has homophilic binding affinity.
source: Fam65b-GFP efficiently co-immunoprecipitated with HA-Fam65b (Figure 8B), demonstrating that Fam65b has homophilic binding affinity.
evidence: This is supported by co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 8B.

claim: Myc-N1 and Myc-C1 both interacted with full-length Fam65b-GFP.
source: Myc-N1 and Myc-C1 both interacted with full-length Fam65b-GFP (Figure 8C), indicating that there are at least two binding sites in Fam65b that mediate homophilic interactions.
evidence: This is supported by co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 8C.

claim: There are at least two binding sites in Fam65b that mediate homophilic interactions.
source: Myc-N1 and Myc-C1 both interacted with full-length Fam65b-GFP (Figure 8C), indicating that there are at least two binding sites in Fam65b that mediate homophilic interactions.
evidence: This is inferred from the co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 8C.

claim: Myc-N1 efficiently interacted with N1-GFP and N2-GFP but not with C1-GFP or C2-GFP.
source: Myc-N1 efficiently interacted with N1-GFP and N2-GFP but not with C1-GFP or C2-GFP (Figure 8D–G).
evidence: This is supported by co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 8D-G.

claim: Myc-C1 efficiently interacted with C1-GFP and C2-GFP but not with N1-GFP or N2-GFP.
source: Likewise Myc-C1 efficiently interacted with C1-GFP and C2-GFP but not with N1-GFP or N2-GFP (Figure 8D–G).
evidence: This is supported by co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 8D-G.

claim: Fam65b molecules can interact with each other via their N-termini and via their C-termini, which could lead to the formation of concatemers.
source: We thus conclude that Fam65b molecules can interact with each other via their N-termini and via their C-termini, which could lead to the formation of concatemers.
evidence: This is inferred from the co-immunoprecipitation data and includes speculation about concatemer formation.

claim: N2-GFP significantly reduced interactions between Fam65b-GFP and Myc-N1.
source: Co-immunoprecipitation experiments demonstrated that N2-GFP significantly reduced interactions between Fam65b-GFP and Myc-N1 (Figure 8H).
evidence: This is supported by co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 8H.

claim: Bundle morphology was severely disrupted by overexpression of N2-GFP in hair cells.
source: Significantly, while Fam65b-GFP did not affect the morphology of hair bundles (Figure 8I,J), bundle morphology was severely disrupted by overexpression of N2-GFP (Figure 8I,J).
evidence: This is supported by injectoporation experiments shown in Figure 8I,J.

claim: Homophilic interactions between Fam65b molecules are required for Fam65b function in hair cells.
source: The data suggest that homophilic interactions between Fam65b molecules are required for Fam65b function in hair cells, although we cannot exclude that N2-GFP might have affected interactions with other proteins as well.
evidence: This is inferred from the dominant negative experiments, with acknowledgment of alternative interpretations.

claim: RhoC was recovered 28 times and RhoA 1 time in yeast-two-hybrid screens with full-length Fam65b as bait.
source: We screened more than 2 million transformants and identified 50 positive clones. Sequencing of the clones revealed that we had recovered RhoC 28 times and RhoA 1 time (data not shown).
evidence: This is based on yeast-two-hybrid screening data.

claim: RhoA has been previously shown to be a binding partner for Fam65b.
source: In fact, RhoA has been previously shown to be a binding partner for Fam65b (Gao et al., 2015; Rougerie et al., 2013), but interactions with RhoC have not been evaluated so far.
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Fam65b bound highly efficiently to RhoC, weakly to RhoA, and not at all to Rac1 and Cdc42.
source: Fam65b bound highly efficiently to RhoC, weakly to RhoA, and not at all to Rac1 and Cdc42 (Figure 9A).
evidence: This is supported by co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 9A.

claim: RhoC was localized near the base of stereocilia and its distribution largely overlapped with the distribution of Fam65b.
source: Remarkably, RhoC was localized near the base of stereocilia and its distribution largely overlapped with the distribution of Fam65b (Figure 9B).
evidence: This is supported by injectoporation and immunolocalization experiments shown in Figure 9B.

claim: Homophilic interactions between Fam65b molecules were strongly enhanced by RhoC.
source: Significantly, homophilic interactions between Fam65b molecules were strongly enhanced by RhoC (Figure 9C,D).
evidence: This is supported by co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 9C,D.

claim: Interactions between Fam65b-GFP and Myc-N1 but not Myc-C1 were strongly enhanced by RhoC.
source: Interactions between Fam65b-GFP and Myc-N1 but not Myc-C1 were strongly enhanced by RhoC (Figure 9E,F), suggesting that RhoC facilitates interactions between the N-terminal of Fam65b.
evidence: This is supported by co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 9E,F.

claim: RhoC facilitates interactions between the N-terminal of Fam65b.
source: Interactions between Fam65b-GFP and Myc-N1 but not Myc-C1 were strongly enhanced by RhoC (Figure 9E,F), suggesting that RhoC facilitates interactions between the N-terminal of Fam65b.
evidence: This is inferred from the co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 9E,F.

claim: Fam65b acts downstream of RhoC, where RhoC regulates Fam65b oligomerization by promoting interactions between the N-termini of Fam65b molecules.
source: These data suggest that Fam65b acts downstream of RhoC, where RhoC regulates Fam65b oligomerization by promoting interactions between the N-termini of Fam65b molecules.
evidence: This is inferred from the biochemical data on RhoC-mediated enhancement of Fam65b oligomerization.

claim: The RL/AA mutation significantly abolished binding of Fam65b to RhoC.
source: Notably, the RL/AA mutation significantly abolished binding of Fam65b to RhoC (Figure 9G).
evidence: This is supported by co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 9G.

claim: RhoC no longer enhanced interactions between Fam65bRL/AA-GFP and Myc-N1.
source: As predicted, while RhoC strongly enhanced homophilic interactions between wild-type Fam65b-GFP and Myc-N1, it no longer enhanced interactions between Fam65bRL/AA-GFP and Myc-N1 (Figure 9H,I).
evidence: This is supported by co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 9H,I.

claim: The RL/AA mutation appeared to reduce the basal homophilic binding activity of Fam65b that is observed without expression of RhoC.
source: In fact, the mutation appeared to even reduce the basal homophilic binding activity of Fam65b that is observed without expression of RhoC (Figure 9H,I).
evidence: This is supported by co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 9H,I.

claim: Fam65b-GFP was efficiently targeted to the basal region of hair cell stereocilia and rescued the morphological hair bundle defect of OHCs from Fam65b-deficient mice.
source: Following injectoporation, Fam65b-GFP was efficiently targeted to the basal region of hair cell stereocilia and rescued the morphological hair bundle defect of OHCs from Fam65b-deficient mice, which formed the typical V-shape (Figure 9J,K).
evidence: This is supported by injectoporation and rescue experiments shown in Figure 9J,K.

claim: Fam65bRL/AA could not rescue the morphological hair bundle defect in hair cells from Fam65b-deficient mice.
source: In contrast, Fam65bRL/AA could not rescue the morphological hair bundle defect in hair cells from Fam65b-deficient mice (Figure 9J,K).
evidence: This is supported by injectoporation and rescue experiments shown in Figure 9J,K.

claim: Binding of Fam65b to RhoC is critical for its function in mechanosensory hair cells.
source: We thus conclude that binding of Fam65b to RhoC is critical for its function in mechanosensory hair cells.
evidence: This is inferred from the rescue experiments showing that the RL/AA mutant cannot rescue hair bundle defects.

claim: The basal domain of stereocilia has been recognized as a specialized compartment with a distinct lipid and protein composition.
source: The basal domain of stereocilia has been recognized as a specialized compartment with a distinct lipid and protein composition and a critical function in mechanotransduction because stereocilia form at their base a taper that allows them to pivot in response to mechanical stimulation (Fettiplace and Kim, 2014; Müller and Barr-Gillespie, 2015; Zhao and Müller, 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: The basal domain of stereocilia has a critical function in mechanotransduction because stereocilia form at their base a taper that allows them to pivot in response to mechanical stimulation.
source: The basal domain of stereocilia has been recognized as a specialized compartment with a distinct lipid and protein composition and a critical function in mechanotransduction because stereocilia form at their base a taper that allows them to pivot in response to mechanical stimulation (Fettiplace and Kim, 2014; Müller and Barr-Gillespie, 2015; Zhao and Müller, 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Taperin binds to distinct proteins and is distributed within the basal domain through the core of each stereocilium.
source: In contrast, taperin binds to distinct proteins and is distributed within the basal domain through the core of each stereocilium.
evidence: This is supported by STORM imaging and biochemical data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Taperin distribution is disrupted in the Fam65b-deficient hair cells.
source: Taperin distribution is disrupted in the Fam65b-deficient hair cells suggesting a potential functional interaction between taperin and Fam65b, but our biochemical data suggest that Fam65b and taperin do not interact directly.
evidence: This is supported by immunolocalization data in mutant mice.

claim: Fam65b and taperin do not interact directly.
source: Taperin distribution is disrupted in the Fam65b-deficient hair cells suggesting a potential functional interaction between taperin and Fam65b, but our biochemical data suggest that Fam65b and taperin do not interact directly.
evidence: This is supported by co-immunoprecipitation and yeast-two-hybrid data.

claim: Fam65b has a critical function in the maintenance of the basal domain of stereocilia.
source: We therefore conclude that Fam65b has a critical function in the maintenance of the basal domain of stereocilia, and that defects in this process likely are the underlying cause of deafness in humans and mice with mutations in the Fam65b gene.
evidence: This is inferred from the morphological and functional data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Defects in the maintenance of the basal domain of stereocilia likely are the underlying cause of deafness in humans and mice with mutations in the Fam65b gene.
source: We therefore conclude that Fam65b has a critical function in the maintenance of the basal domain of stereocilia, and that defects in this process likely are the underlying cause of deafness in humans and mice with mutations in the Fam65b gene.
evidence: This is inferred from the data and includes speculation about the mechanism of deafness.

claim: Fam65b-deficient mice are deaf already at 4 weeks of age.
source: We show here that Fam65b-deficient mice similarly are deaf already at 4 weeks of age, the first time point analyzed.
evidence: This is supported by ABR measurements.

claim: Defects in hair cell survival is not the primary cause of the auditory phenotype in mice lacking Fam65b.
source: However, we did not observed defects in hair cell survival at 2 and 4 weeks after birth, suggesting that the death of hair cells is not the primary cause of the auditory phenotype in mice lacking Fam65b.
evidence: This is inferred from the hair cell counts showing no significant loss.

claim: Defects in hair bundle morphology in Fam65b-deficient mice are manifest prior to the onset of hearing in mice.
source: In Fam65b-deficient mice, we observe defects in hair bundle morphology already in the first few days after birth suggesting that degenerative changes are manifest prior to the onset of hearing in mice.
evidence: This is supported by morphological analysis at P2 and P5.

claim: The structural defects in Fam65b-deficient hair cells are associated with defects in mechanotransduction.
source: The structural defects are associated with defects in mechanotransduction, indicating functional defects in hair cells that likely cause the auditory phenotype of the mutant mice.
evidence: This is supported by electrophysiological recordings.

claim: Defects in hair cells are critical for the auditory phenotype caused by Fam65b mutations.
source: While our findings suggest that defects in hair cells are critical for the auditory phenotype caused by Fam65b mutations, we also observed Fam65b expression in the microvilli of supporting cells including Hensen's cells and it cannot be excluded that defects in their development and function might contribute to the auditory phenotype.
evidence: This is inferred from the expression pattern and functional data, with acknowledgment of alternative possibilities.

claim: Defects in hair bundles of hair cells are likely cell-autonomous.
source: Regardless of the involvement of supporting cells, defects in hair bundles of hair cells are likely cell-autonomous because we can induce them by knock-down of Fam65b expression in hair cells (Figure 4) and rescue them by re-expression of Fam65b in Fam65b-deficient hair cells (Figure 5).
evidence: This is inferred from the shRNA knockdown and rescue experiments.

claim: The acute rescue of hair cell morphology by re-expression of Fam65b at postnatal ages suggests that defects in hair bundle morphology are likely not a secondary consequence of perturbations in an overall developmental program.
source: The acute rescue of hair cell morphology by re-expression of Fam65b at postnatal ages also suggests that defects in hair bundle morphology are likely not a secondary consequence of perturbations in an overall developmental program but are more specifically linked to a role of Fam65b in stereocilia.
evidence: This is inferred from the rescue experiments and includes interpretation of the mechanism.

claim: Fam65b might have a PX-BAR domain that can associate with membranes.
source: Membrane-targeting was mainly inferred previously because sequence comparison indicated that Fam65b might have a PX-BAR domain that can associate with membranes (Diaz-Horta et al., 2014; Farooq and Tekin, 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: The conclusion that Fam65b has a PX-BAR domain was subsequently contested.
source: However, this conclusion was subsequently contested (Teasdale and Collins, 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior research.

claim: Fam65b is concentrated at the basal domain of stereocilia and not localized uniformly along the entire length of stereocilia.
source: Using STORM microscopy, we have now refined the localization of Fam65b within stereocilia and demonstrate that it is concentrated at their basal domain and not localized uniformly along the entire length of stereocilia.
evidence: This is supported by STORM imaging data.

claim: Fam65b is localized in a circumferential ring near the stereociliary base and does not penetrate the core of stereocilia.
source: In addition, we show that Fam65b is localized in a circumferential ring near the stereociliary base and does not penetrate the core of stereocilia.
evidence: This is supported by STORM imaging data.

claim: Fam65b can bind to RhoA and inhibit its function.
source: Previous studies have shown that Fam65b can bind to RhoA and inhibit its function (Gao et al., 2015; Rougerie et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Fam65b binds much more strongly to RhoC than to RhoA.
source: We show here that Fam65b binds much more strongly to RhoC than to RhoA but we did not observe effects of Fam65b on RhoC activity.
evidence: This is supported by co-immunoprecipitation data.

claim: Fam65b did not have effects on RhoC activity.
source: We show here that Fam65b binds much more strongly to RhoC than to RhoA but we did not observe effects of Fam65b on RhoC activity.
evidence: This is based on biochemical assays.

claim: Oligomerization of Fam65b is driven by interactions between the N-termini of Fam65b, which are promoted by RhoC, and by interactions between the C-termini.
source: Oligomerization is driven by interactions between the N-termini of Fam65b, which are promoted by RhoC, and by interactions between the C-termini suggesting that Fam65b monomers can assemble into extended filaments.
evidence: This is supported by co-immunoprecipitation data.

claim: Fam65b monomers can assemble into extended filaments.
source: Oligomerization is driven by interactions between the N-termini of Fam65b, which are promoted by RhoC, and by interactions between the C-termini suggesting that Fam65b monomers can assemble into extended filaments.
evidence: This is inferred from the oligomerization data.

claim: STORM imaging of Fam65b following its expression in heterologous cells suggests that oligomerization leads to linear filaments that can also bend into ring-like structures similar to those observed in hair cells.
source: In fact, STORM imaging of Fam65b following its expression in heterologous cells (data not shown) suggests that oligomerization leads to linear filaments that can also bend into ring-like structures similar to those observed in hair cells.
evidence: This is based on STORM imaging in heterologous cells.

claim: Fam65b oligomers might form spring-like structures near the membrane at the base of stereocilia that affect the mechanical properties of the bundle.
source: One interesting possibility would be that Fam65b oligomers form spring-like structures near the membrane at the base of stereocilia that affect the mechanical properties of the bundle.
evidence: This is speculative interpretation of the data.

claim: Taperin has a distribution in hair cells different from Fam65b.
source: Our STORM imaging data further provide evidence that taperin has a distribution in hair cells different from Fam65b.
evidence: This is supported by STORM imaging data.

claim: Only taperin is localized within the core of stereocilia while Fam65b forms a circumferential ring.
source: While both proteins are localized near the base of stereocilia, only taperin is localized within the core of stereocilia. Fam65b instead forms a circumferential ring.
evidence: This is supported by STORM imaging data.

claim: The diameter of the domain occupied by taperin and of the Fam65b ring are similar, raising the possibility that the two compartments show partially overlap.
source: The diameter of the domain occupied by taperin and of the Fam65b ring are similar, raising the possibility that the two compartments show partially overlap.
evidence: This is based on measurements from STORM images and includes speculation.

claim: Taperin localization is perturbed in the absence of Fam65b, suggesting that the distribution of protein complexes containing Fam65b and taperin is interdependent.
source: Taperin localization is perturbed in the absence of Fam65b, suggesting that the distribution of protein complexes containing Fam65b and taperin is interdependent.
evidence: This is inferred from the immunolocalization data in mutant mice.

claim: Mutations in Fam65b cause deafness at least in part by affecting stereocilia morphogenesis and function.
source: Regardless, our data strongly suggest that Fam65b expression and oligomerization is critical for maintaining the structural organization of the basal domain of stereocilia and that mutations in Fam65b cause deafness at least in part by affecting stereocilia morphogenesis and function.
evidence: This is inferred from the morphological and functional data.

claim: Re-expression of Fam65b in Fam65b-deficient hair cells at postnatal ages rescued their morphological defects.
source: Re-expression of Fam65b in Fam65b-deficient hair cells at postnatal ages rescued their morphological defects, suggesting that it might be possible to repair hair cell damage in human patients with mutations in the FAM65B gene.
evidence: This is supported by rescue experiments and includes speculation about therapeutic potential.

claim: STORM microscopy can be applied successfully to hair cells.
source: Our data show that STORM microscopy can be applied successfully to hair cells and will thus be a useful tool to investigate the spatial organization of proteins in stereocilia in normal and pathological conditions.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the successful application of STORM in this study.
